title: Add interactive RAG lab: guided scenario walkthroughs and lightweight eval kit
author: Priya Shah
description: Motivation: Provide a compact, opinionated 'RAG lab' tailored for developer onboarding and rapid iteration. This PR adds a set of guided micro-scenarios, VS Code snippets, a tiny local eval harness, and a reproducible playbook to help engineers test RAG agent/tool-calling flows end-to-end locally. The goal is low cognitive overhead: one folder that demonstrates common pitfalls (tool timeouts, partial retrievals, hallucination checks) and shows recommended Redwood configs (batching, kv-cache hints, model pinning). Changes include interactive walkthroughs (markdown playbooks), a lightweight eval script that runs a small suite of prompts against a local dev endpoint, example tool adapters (http-fetch, sqlite-qa stub), developer-focused VS Code snippets for rapid authoring, and docs updates linking to the new lab. Checklist: [x] add playbook scenarios, [x] add eval harness and runner script, [x] add vscode snippets and README guidance, [x] add CI smoke test for example repo, [x] update docs site reference and sidebar, [x] include linear tickets in PR metadata. Usage: clone examples/rag-lab, follow README to run the local shim (docker-less), invoke scripts/run_eval.sh to run the included prompt set against either the Redwood hosted sandbox or a locally proxied devstack. Evaluation: the harness reports token counts, latency percentiles, and a simple precision-style check against golden answers for retrieval-based QA. Backwards compatibility: non-breaking; examples are opt-in. Related: ENG-1982 (RAG developer ramp), PR #52319 (aws stepfunction examples) for orchestration inspiration.
